learningObjective: Explain why one target-model pass can verify several drafted positions at near the latency of one decode step when target inference is limited by reading weights rather than arithmetic.
mediumRationale: A paired semantic cost ledger is the smallest medium that can hold the target weight traffic constant while contrasting one-token decode with K-position verification, without duplicating the existing first-rejection token trace.

mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected because two responsive panels can compare identical target-weight reads, different useful token work, and the condition under which latency remains similar using direct labels and ordinary reading order.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because a K or hardware sweep would require measured bandwidth, batch size, kernels, cache behavior, and draft cost not supplied by the article; invented timings would weaken the conditional claim.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the foundational papers contain algorithm and performance figures, but the learning objective needs an original qualitative cost ledger and public arXiv access is not treated as figure-adaptation permission.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the phrase 'essentially free' is easy to misread as zero computation. Readers need to see that target weight traffic stays roughly fixed while useful arithmetic increases, and that the argument applies only while the pass remains memory-bound.

pages.insight: The compute-optimization setup defines memory-bound execution through arithmetic intensity and the gap between HBM bandwidth and tensor-core throughput, supplying the hardware premise.
The preceding slide covers sparse, low-rank, and dilated attention; it changes long-context attention math rather than decode-time weight amortization.

The speculative-decoding slide states that single-token target passes are memory-bound and that one parallel K-token target pass reuses the same weight loading, but presents the cost argument only in prose.

The following mixed-precision slide explains that fewer bytes can accelerate memory-bound operations, reinforcing bandwidth sensitivity but changing representation size rather than tokens per weight read.
The training-and-serving summary identifies speculative decoding as the remedy for autoregressive serial dependence and distinguishes it from quantization, paging, and continuous batching.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is why parallel verification is cheap without being computationally free. In low-batch decode, the target must stream its weights from HBM to produce one next-token distribution, while matrix-vector work may leave compute units underused. Scoring a short drafted block still reads the target weights once but performs useful work for multiple positions, raising arithmetic intensity. Latency can therefore remain near one target step only while the larger operation still fits the bandwidth-bound regime; draft generation, acceptance handling, cache management, and eventual compute saturation remain real costs. The original ledger makes no universal speed or hardware claim.
